thesis: Strategy v1 (November 11, 2026), Tuesday November 17 premarket review at 2026-11-17T13:30:15.361Z. The independently recorded November 12 SPY BUY (decision stock_20261112_autonom) filled prospectively on November 12 at a modeled $754.35697046 per share, with a $0.15 fee; no pending stock orders remain and there is no duplicate November 17 decision. The latest successfully collected COMPLETED stock bar is November 16, not a live November 17 executable quote: SPY opened $749.66 and closed $739.95, versus November 13 $754.37 and the original buy thesis's $735.29 November 6 review threshold. SPY is now only about 0.63% above that threshold; importantly the original observable reconsideration condition was TWO subsequent completed closes below $735.29 alongside deteriorating breadth, and that condition has not occurred. The November 16 close marks the existing SPY position near $147.14; cash remains $849.85; portfolio value $996.985251 versus the common-date $964.971785 passive SPY benchmark. This $32.01 advantage is overwhelmingly attributable to approximately 85% cash exposure during a declining market, NOT evidence of an effective market-timing signal. Relative to the November 12 SPY entry, the position has lost roughly $2.86 in mark-to-market value; a new sale would incur another modeled 0.10% fee and 0.05% adverse slippage. The 4–8 week diversified exposure rationale is still intelligible, and the allocation is small enough to tolerate short-run volatility without asserting a forecast. However, Reuters and AP November 16 reporting document a broad equity decline (S&P 500 about -1.9%, Nasdaq about -2.5%) driven by AI/semiconductor uncertainty, possible tighter China chip-access rules, valuation pressure, and hawkish-rate concerns. Reuters November 17 premarket reporting notes Nvidia earnings after today's close and exceptionally large implied earnings uncertainty, while AP describes mixed futures and a partial Nasdaq rebound. These are time-stamped market indications, not November 17 completed bars or executable SPY prices; do not preempt the earnings result. Relative alternatives: RSP equal-weight would reduce megacap concentration but its November 16 close $218.93 and weakness do not establish better near-term breadth; IWM $272.94 adds smaller-company/rate sensitivity; QQQ $661.75 is more exposed to the very AI technology shock; XLE $63.69 and XLV $187.88 require sector-specific tilts without independent supported expected-return cases; SGOV $100.58 is a defensive rate reference but the simulator does not yet model its distributions, making cash a cleaner defensive alternative. No untracked or illiquid candidate is proposed. Review after Nvidia's actual report and two further completed SPY sessions: if two closes fall below $735.29 with broad deterioration, or materially adverse inflation/rate/earnings evidence undermines diversified exposure, consider reducing or exiting the $147 SPY holding; if breadth stabilizes, reconsider a modest addition subject to the 35% cap and prospective execution. HOLD incurs no new trading costs and preserves the original modest market exposure while retaining cash optionality. No claim of profitable timing, live prices, or new fill.
